paragraphs.text: Putting away therefore all wickedness, and all guile, and hypocrisies, and envies, and all evil speakings,
paragraphs.original: Ἀποθέμενοι οὖν πᾶσαν κακίαν καὶ πάντα δόλον καὶ ὑποκρίσεις καὶ φθόνους καὶ πάσας καταλαλιάς,
paragraphs.translit: Apothemenoi oun pasan kakian kai panta dolon kai hypokriseis kai phthonous kai pasas katalalias,

paragraphs.text: as newborn babes, long for the spiritual milk which is without guile, that ye may grow thereby unto salvation;
paragraphs.original: ὡς ἀρτιγέννητα βρέφη τὸ λογικὸν ἄδολον γάλα ἐπιποθήσατε, ἵνα ἐν αὐτῷ αὐξηθῆτε εἰς σωτηρίαν,
paragraphs.translit: hōs artigennēta brephē to logikon adolon gala epipothēsate, hina en autō auxēthēte eis sōtērian,

paragraphs.text: if ye have tasted that the Lord is gracious:
paragraphs.original: εἰ ἐγεύσασθε ὅτι χρηστὸς ὁ κύριος.
paragraphs.translit: ei egeusasthe hoti chrēstos ho kyrios.

paragraphs.text: unto whom coming, a living stone, rejected indeed of men, but with God elect, precious,
paragraphs.original: Πρὸς ὃν προσερχόμενοι, λίθον ζῶντα, ὑπὸ ἀνθρώπων μὲν ἀποδεδοκιμασμένον παρὰ δὲ θεῷ ἐκλεκτὸν ἔντιμον
paragraphs.translit: Pros hon proserchomenoi, lithon zōnta, hypo anthrōpōn men apodedokimasmenon para de theō eklekton entimon

paragraphs.text: ye also, as living stones, are built up a spiritual house, to be a holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices, acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.
paragraphs.original: καὶ αὐτοὶ ὡς λίθοι ζῶντες οἰκοδομεῖσθε οἶκος πνευματικὸς εἰς ἱεράτευμα ἅγιον, ἀνενέγκαι πνευματικὰς θυσίας εὐπροσδέκτους θεῷ διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: kai autoi hōs lithoi zōntes oikodomeisthe oikos pneumatikos eis hierateuma hagion, anenenkai pneumatikas thysias euprosdektous theō dia Iēsou Christou·

paragraphs.text: Because it is contained in scripture, Behold, I lay in Zion a chief corner stone, elect, precious: And he that believeth on him shall not be put to shame.
paragraphs.original: διότι περιέχει ἐν γραφῇ· Ἰδοὺ τίθημι ἐν Σιὼν λίθον ἀκρογωνιαῖον ἐκλεκτὸν ἔντιμον, καὶ ὁ πιστεύων ἐπʼ αὐτῷ οὐ μὴ καταισχυνθῇ.
paragraphs.translit: dioti periechei en graphē· Idou tithēmi en Siōn lithon akrogōniaion eklekton entimon, kai ho pisteuōn epʼ autō ou mē kataischynthē.

paragraphs.text: For you therefore that believe is the preciousness: but for such as disbelieve, The stone which the builders rejected, The same was made the head of the corner;
paragraphs.original: ὑμῖν οὖν ἡ τιμὴ τοῖς πιστεύουσιν· ἀπιστοῦσιν δὲ λίθος ὃν ἀπεδοκίμασαν οἱ οἰκοδομοῦντες οὗτος ἐγενήθη εἰς κεφαλὴν γωνίας
paragraphs.translit: hymin oun hē timē tois pisteuousin· apistousin de lithos hon apedokimasan hoi oikodomountes houtos egenēthē eis kephalēn gōnias

paragraphs.text: and, A stone of stumbling, and a rock of offence;     for they stumble at the word, being disobedient: whereunto also they were appointed.
paragraphs.original: καὶ λίθος προσκόμματος καὶ πέτρα σκανδάλου· οἳ προσκόπτουσιν τῷ λόγῳ ἀπειθοῦντες· εἰς ὃ καὶ ἐτέθησαν.
paragraphs.translit: kai lithos proskommatos kai petra skandalou· hoi proskoptousin tō logō apeithountes· eis ho kai etethēsan.

paragraphs.text: But ye are a elect race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for [God`s] own possession, that ye may show forth the excellencies of him who called you out of darkness into his marvellous light:
paragraphs.original: Ὑμεῖς δὲ γένος ἐκλεκτόν, βασίλειον ἱεράτευμα, ἔθνος ἅγιον, λαὸς εἰς περιποίησιν, ὅπως τὰς ἀρετὰς ἐξαγγείλητε τοῦ ἐκ σκότους ὑμᾶς καλέσαντος εἰς τὸ θαυμαστὸν αὐτοῦ φῶς·
paragraphs.translit: Hymeis de genos eklekton, basileion hierateuma, ethnos hagion, laos eis peripoiēsin, hopōs tas aretas exangeilēte tou ek skotous hymas kalesantos eis to thaumaston autou phōs·

paragraphs.text: who in time past were no people, but now are the people of God: who had not obtained mercy, but now have obtained mercy.
paragraphs.original: οἵ ποτε οὐ λαὸς νῦν δὲ λαὸς θεοῦ, οἱ οὐκ ἠλεημένοι νῦν δὲ ἐλεηθέντες.
paragraphs.translit: hoi pote ou laos nyn de laos theou, hoi ouk ēleēmenoi nyn de eleēthentes.

paragraphs.text: Beloved, I beseech you as sojourners and pilgrims, to abstain from fleshly lust, which war against the soul;
paragraphs.original: Ἀγαπητοί, παρακαλῶ ὡς παροίκους καὶ παρεπιδήμους ἀπέχεσθαι τῶν σαρκικῶν ἐπιθυμιῶν, αἵτινες στρατεύονται κατὰ τῆς ψυχῆς·
paragraphs.translit: Agapētoi, parakalō hōs paroikous kai parepidēmous apechesthai tōn sarkikōn epithymiōn, haitines strateuontai kata tēs psychēs·

paragraphs.text: having your behavior seemly among the Gentiles; that, wherein they speak against you as evil-doers, they may by your good works, which they behold, glorify God in the day of visitation.
paragraphs.original: τὴν ἀναστροφὴν ὑμῶν ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν ἔχοντες καλήν, ἵνα, ἐν ᾧ καταλαλοῦσιν ὑμῶν ὡς κακοποιῶν, ἐκ τῶν καλῶν ἔργων ἐποπτεύοντες δοξάσωσι τὸν θεὸν ἐν ἡμέρᾳ ἐπισκοπῆς.
paragraphs.translit: tēn anastrophēn hymōn en tois ethnesin echontes kalēn, hina, en hō katalalousin hymōn hōs kakopoiōn, ek tōn kalōn ergōn epopteuontes doxasōsi ton theon en hēmera episkopēs.

paragraphs.text: Be subject to every ordinance of man for the Lord`s sake: whether to the king, as supreme;
paragraphs.original: Ὑποτάγητε πάσῃ ἀνθρωπίνῃ κτίσει διὰ τὸν κύριον· εἴτε βασιλεῖ ὡς ὑπερέχοντι,
paragraphs.translit: Hypotagēte pasē anthrōpinē ktisei dia ton kyrion· eite basilei hōs hyperechonti,

paragraphs.text: or unto governors, as sent by him for vengeance on evil-doers and for praise to them that do well.
paragraphs.original: εἴτε ἡγεμόσιν ὡς διʼ αὐτοῦ πεμπομένοις εἰς ἐκδίκησιν κακοποιῶν ἔπαινον δὲ ἀγαθοποιῶν
paragraphs.translit: eite hēgemosin hōs diʼ autou pempomenois eis ekdikēsin kakopoiōn epainon de agathopoiōn

paragraphs.text: For so is the will of God, that by well-doing ye should put to silence the ignorance of foolish men:
paragraphs.original: (ὅτι οὕτως ἐστὶν τὸ θέλημα τοῦ θεοῦ, ἀγαθοποιοῦντας φιμοῦν τὴν τῶν ἀφρόνων ἀνθρώπων ἀγνωσίαν)·
paragraphs.translit: (hoti houtōs estin to thelēma tou theou, agathopoiountas phimoun tēn tōn aphronōn anthrōpōn agnōsian)·

paragraphs.text: as free, and not using your freedom for a cloak of wickedness, but as bondservants of God.
paragraphs.original: ὡς ἐλεύθεροι, καὶ μὴ ὡς ἐπικάλυμμα ἔχοντες τῆς κακίας τὴν ἐλευθερίαν, ἀλλʼ ὡς θεοῦ δοῦλοι.
paragraphs.translit: hōs eleutheroi, kai mē hōs epikalymma echontes tēs kakias tēn eleutherian, allʼ hōs theou douloi.

paragraphs.text: Honor all men. Love the brotherhood. Fear God. Honor the king.
paragraphs.original: πάντας τιμήσατε, τὴν ἀδελφότητα ἀγαπᾶτε, τὸν θεὸν φοβεῖσθε, τὸν βασιλέα τιμᾶτε.
paragraphs.translit: pantas timēsate, tēn adelphotēta agapate, ton theon phobeisthe, ton basilea timate.

paragraphs.text: Servants, [be] in subjection to your masters with all fear; not only to the good and gentle, but also to the froward.
paragraphs.original: Οἱ οἰκέται ὑποτασσόμενοι ἐν παντὶ φόβῳ τοῖς δεσπόταις, οὐ μόνον τοῖς ἀγαθοῖς καὶ ἐπιεικέσιν ἀλλὰ καὶ τοῖς σκολιοῖς.
paragraphs.translit: Hoi oiketai hypotassomenoi en panti phobō tois despotais, ou monon tois agathois kai epieikesin alla kai tois skoliois.

paragraphs.text: For this is acceptable, if for conscience toward God a man endureth griefs, suffering wrongfully.
paragraphs.original: τοῦτο γὰρ χάρις εἰ διὰ συνείδησιν θεοῦ ὑποφέρει τις λύπας πάσχων ἀδίκως·
paragraphs.translit: touto gar charis ei dia syneidēsin theou hypopherei tis lypas paschōn adikōs·

paragraphs.text: For what glory is it, if, when ye sin, and are buffeted [for it], ye shall take it patiently? but if, when ye do well, and suffer [for it], ye shall take it patiently, this is acceptable with God.
paragraphs.original: ποῖον γὰρ κλέος εἰ ἁμαρτάνοντες καὶ κολαφιζόμενοι ὑπομενεῖτε; ἀλλʼ εἰ ἀγαθοποιοῦντες καὶ πάσχοντες ὑπομενεῖτε, τοῦτο χάρις παρὰ θεῷ.
paragraphs.translit: poion gar kleos ei hamartanontes kai kolaphizomenoi hypomeneite; allʼ ei agathopoiountes kai paschontes hypomeneite, touto charis para theō.

paragraphs.text: For hereunto were ye called: because Christ also suffered for you, leaving you an example, that ye should follow his steps:
paragraphs.original: εἰς τοῦτο γὰρ ἐκλήθητε, ὅτι καὶ Χριστὸς ἔπαθεν ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν, ὑμῖν ὑπολιμπάνων ὑπογραμμὸν ἵνα ἐπακολουθήσητε τοῖς ἴχνεσιν αὐτοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: eis touto gar eklēthēte, hoti kai Christos epathen hyper hymōn, hymin hypolimpanōn hypogrammon hina epakolouthēsēte tois ichnesin autou·

paragraphs.text: who did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth:
paragraphs.original: ὃς ἁμαρτίαν οὐκ ἐποίησεν οὐδὲ εὑρέθη δόλος ἐν τῷ στόματι αὐτοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: hos hamartian ouk epoiēsen oude heurethē dolos en tō stomati autou·

paragraphs.text: who, when he was reviled, reviled not again; when he suffered threatened not; but committed [himself] to him that judgeth righteously:
paragraphs.original: ὃς λοιδορούμενος οὐκ ἀντελοιδόρει, πάσχων οὐκ ἠπείλει, παρεδίδου δὲ τῷ κρίνοντι δικαίως·
paragraphs.translit: hos loidoroumenos ouk anteloidorei, paschōn ouk ēpeilei, paredidou de tō krinonti dikaiōs·

paragraphs.text: who his own self bare our sins in his body upon the tree, that we, having died unto sins, might live unto righteousness; by whose stripes ye were healed.
paragraphs.original: ὃς τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶν αὐτὸς ἀνήνεγκεν ἐν τῷ σώματι αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὸ ξύλον, ἵνα ταῖς ἁμαρτίαις ἀπογενόμενοι τῇ δικαιοσύνῃ ζήσωμεν· οὗ τῷ μώλωπι ἰάθητε.
paragraphs.translit: hos tas hamartias hēmōn autos anēnenken en tō sōmati autou epi to xylon, hina tais hamartiais apogenomenoi tē dikaiosynē zēsōmen· hou tō mōlōpi iathēte.

paragraphs.text: For ye were going astray like sheep; but are now returned unto the Shepherd and Bishop of your souls.
paragraphs.original: ἦτε γὰρ ὡς πρόβατα πλανώμενοι, ἀλλὰ ἐπεστράφητε νῦν ἐπὶ τὸν ποιμένα καὶ ἐπίσκοπον τῶν ψυχῶν ὑμῶν.
paragraphs.translit: ēte gar hōs probata planōmenoi, alla epestraphēte nyn epi ton poimena kai episkopon tōn psychōn hymōn.
